settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile resolves the destination via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) (line 309), which is used in an attempt to prevent simple '../' path traversal; placeholders for traversal defense exist but were not verifiable.
The symlink is only created when symlinkDestination is non-empty (line 325); entries without link names fall to directory/file handling.
There is an explicit comment at line 308 ('Symlinks re-evaluate back to the original file here. Unsure if this is a good thing...') indicating the authors were aware this path deserves scrutiny.
This snapshot is version 3.6.0-SNAPSHOT (pom.xml:13); later releases are reported to harden symlink handling, so behavior may differ from this tree.
candidates.description: AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile (src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/archiver/AbstractUnArchiver.java:303-361) is the shared extraction primitive for TAR and ZIP unarchivers. At line 309 it computes the target as FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName), then if the entry supplies a symlink destination (line 325) it calls SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink(f, new File(symlinkDestination)) at line 327. The symlinkDestination string originates directly from untrusted archive metadata and is not checked for absolute paths, '..' segments, or containment within the destination directory. For non-directory, non-symlink entries the same f path is opened with new FileOutputStream(f) at line 338 and populated from the archive stream at line 340. Because the symlink is created first and later entries are resolved by the same routine, an archive can create a symlink whose target lies outside dir and then include a subsequent entry whose resolved path traverses that symlink, causing content to be written outside the intended extraction root. Upstream (TarUnArchiver.java:112-114, AbstractZipUnArchiver.java:176-181 and 235-253) passes archive-controlled entry names and link names into this routine without additional validation, and no containment/validation logic for link destinations appears anywhere in the extraction paths.
missing_evidence: Source of plexus-utils 3.1.0 FileUtils.resolveFile was not available in this repository, so it cannot be confirmed whether canonicalization would reject a path that traverses a previously created symlink.
No test in the allowed source spans demonstrates extraction of a malicious archive with symlink entries.
SymlinkUtils.createSymbolicLink implementation (plexus-io) was not inspected, so it is unknown whether it silently refuses unsafe link targets.
The effective value of isOverwrite() / whether symlinks are disabled by configuration in real callers was not traced.
preconditions: The application extracts an archive supplied or influenced by an untrusted party.
The archive contains a symbolic-link entry followed by a file entry whose path traverses the created link (or a link entry pointing to an absolute/outside path).
The unarchiver runs with filesystem permissions that allow creating files outside the destination directory.
candidates.title: Symlink entry destination is not validated in AbstractUnArchiver.extractFile, allowing writes through a symlink pointing outside the extraction directory

counter_evidence: The downstream extractFile still calls FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName) (AbstractUnArchiver.java:309), which is the primary traversal defense and is applied regardless of the prefix check.
Both execute() overloads reject nothing but rely on the same extractFile; the prefix check is an inclusion filter, not the security boundary.
No evidence was found that any caller passes attacker-controlled 'path' values.
candidates.description: AbstractZipUnArchiver.execute(String path, File outputDirectory) (src/main/java/org/codehaus/plexus/archiver/zip/AbstractZipUnArchiver.java:226-272) selects entries for extraction with ze.getName().startsWith(path) at line 246 before calling extractFileIfIncluded (line 250). A raw string prefix comparison can match unintended entries, e.g. a path of 'foo' also matches 'foobar/evil.txt', and it performs no normalization of './', '..' or absolute components. The selected name is then passed unchanged into the shared extractFile routine (extractFileIfIncluded, lines 217-223), so the effectiveness of entry selection depends entirely on that downstream routine. Compared with the main execute() method (lines 159-202), which extracts every selected entry without a path filter, this overload applies only a weak textual filter.
missing_evidence: Behavior of FileUtils.resolveFile with names containing '..' or absolute path components could not be verified from repository sources.
No callers of the extract(String, File) overload in this tree were inspected to determine whether 'path' is untrusted.
No test exercises the prefix-match edge case.
preconditions: A caller uses the extract(path, outputDirectory) overload with a caller-supplied path prefix.
The archive contains entries whose names coincidentally share the prefix but are outside the intended subtree.
candidates.title: extract(path, outputDirectory) in AbstractZipUnArchiver uses a raw startsWith prefix check on entry names

counter_evidence: Dependency version choices alone do not establish a vulnerability in this repository's source.
The libraries are external and not present in the reviewed tree, so their code paths were not inspected.
candidates.description: pom.xml pins plexus-utils 3.1.0 (lines 57-61), plexus-io 3.0.1 (lines 62-66) and commons-compress 1.16.1 (lines 67-71) and declares Java 7 (line 34). These are old dependency versions with publicly known archive-parsing issues. This is a dependency-hygiene observation about the build metadata only, not a demonstrated vulnerability in this project's own code; the repository does not vendor these libraries, so their internal behavior could not be inspected here.
missing_evidence: No vulnerability triage or exploitability analysis of the pinned third-party versions was performed.
The parent POM (org.codehaus.plexus:plexus:5.0) content is not in this tree, so effective dependency management is unknown.
preconditions: Application packages this library and transitively depends on these specific old library versions.
candidates.title: Windows-based misconfiguration in Maven parent/module build metadata (informational)
